summary: A concise overview of this week's technology developments.

items.title: Warp’s new system is an out-of-the-box software factory for AI development
items.summary: Warp has introduced Warp Factories, a new infrastructure system designed to simplify building AI software factories. This tool aims to streamline the development and deployment of AI-driven software solutions.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot reveals secret input that allowed it to be hacked
items.summary: A vulnerability in Microsoft Copilot allowed hackers to steal passwords when a target clicked on a specific link. The exploit relied on a secret parameter that forced the AI to reveal sensitive information.

items.title: Firefox’s Smart Window promises a better AI browser
items.summary: Mozilla has introduced Smart Window, an AI-powered browsing mode for Firefox that integrates real-time web information and natural language history search. This update enhances user experience by automatically organizing tabs and providing visual page previews.

items.title: OpenAI launches a safer ChatGPT for teens — years after teens started using it
items.summary: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Teens, introducing age-appropriate safety measures and parental controls. The update aims to steer younger users away from harmful content and academic dishonesty.

items.title: Former SpaceX engineers are building a robotic factory for making steel parts
items.summary: Former SpaceX engineers are building a robotic factory dedicated to manufacturing steel parts. The venture focuses on practical automation rather than dogmatically pursuing full autonomy.
